sections.markdown:
## C — Your license to drive, part two: parental approval, the graduated licensing system, the instruction permit, the provisional license and its limits, Vanessa's Law, the under-21 license and the age-fifteen exceptions
Knowledge domain: how a Minnesota teen moves from instruction permit to provisional license to the under-twenty-one Class D license, who may sign for a minor, the supervision, phone, night and passenger limits at each stage, the Vanessa's Law penalties, and the licenses available at age fifteen.

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
An applicant under 18 needs the permit or license application approved by a parent, a guardian appointed by a court, a foster parent appointed by a county, or the director of the transitional living program where the teen lives. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
When the parents are divorced, the custodial parent or a stepparent married to the custodial parent may approve the teen's application. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
A teen with no living parent or guardian, or who is married or legally emancipated, may have a close family member, an employer or a spouse sign, and that signer must be at least 18. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
The person who signed a teen's application may later withdraw that approval. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
Host sponsors of a foreign exchange student may sign only with documented legal guardianship; otherwise the student brings two forms with the parents' notarized signatures, one for the permit and one for the provisional license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
Under the Graduated Driver's Licensing system, a driver aged 18 or younger is required to keep an instruction permit a minimum of six months before the road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
An instruction permit covers two years of practice with a licensed supervising driver in the front passenger seat, practicing without a valid permit is illegal, and the permit must be with you whenever you drive. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
To get a permit you must be at least 15 and either finish 30 hours of classroom instruction while enrolled in behind-the-wheel training, or be in a concurrent course with the first 15 classroom hours done; at 18 or older no driver education is needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
The permit also requires meeting the identification rules, passing the vision screening and the written test, completing an application and paying the permit fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
A permit holder under 18 needs a supervising driver who is 21 or older, all occupants must wear a seat belt or ride in a child restraint, and the teen may not use or talk on a cell phone even hands-free. [A01]
Why it matters: the supervisor age differs for adult permit holders.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A02
A permit holder aged 18 or older may be supervised by a driver aged 18 or older, and everyone in the vehicle must be belted or in a child restraint. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A02
The road test may be taken after six months of practice driving, or after three months for a permit holder aged 19 or older. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
A lost or expired permit is replaced by applying for a new one, which is valid for two years from the day you apply. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
The provisional license is the second stage of graduated licensing, is valid for two years from the application date, and requires every occupant to be belted while banning cell phone use, hands-free included. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
A provisional license requires being at least 16, finishing both the classroom and behind-the-wheel phases of driver education, and holding a permit for six months with no moving, alcohol or controlled-substance convictions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
The supervised driving log must show at least 40 hours including 15 at night if a parent takes the class from an approved driver education program, or at least 50 hours including 15 at night without that class. [A02]
Why it matters: the forty versus fifty hour split is a frequent test item.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A02
The provisional license also requires a passed road test and an application signed by an approved adult such as a parent or guardian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
In the first six months a provisional driver may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. unless with a licensed driver at least 25 years old, driving between home and work or a school event without school transportation, or driving for employment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A03
In the first six months a provisional driver may carry only one passenger under 20 unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A03
In the second six months a provisional driver may carry no more than three passengers under 20 unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A03
Immediate family members under 20 do not count against the provisional passenger limits in either six-month period. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A03
Vanessa's Law, passed a year after Vanessa Weiss died in May 2003 as a passenger of an unlicensed 15-year-old, covers every teen who commits an impaired driving crime or a crash-related moving violation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A03
An unlicensed teen convicted of a crash-related moving violation or an alcohol or drug offense such as DWI, Implied Consent, Open Bottle or the Not a Drop law cannot get any license or permit until age 18. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
After turning 18 that teen must meet the reinstatement requirements, pass the Class D written test, get a permit and hold it at least six months, or three months at 19 or older, before the road test. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A03
A provisional license holder revoked for such a violation cannot regain a license until age 18 or the end of the withdrawal period, whichever comes later. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A04
Reinstatement for that provisional holder usually means serving the withdrawal period, passing the Class D written test, paying a $680 reinstatement fee, finishing a 30-hour classroom course that cannot be taken online, and applying for a permit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A04
After reinstatement the permit is held for 90 days, during which six hours of behind-the-wheel driver education are completed, and then the driver applies for a license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A04
An under-21 Class D license requires being at least 18, or holding a provisional license for 12 consecutive months with no alcohol, controlled-substance or crash-related moving violation convictions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A04
An under-21 license applicant is limited to at most one conviction for a non-crash moving violation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A04
An applicant under 18 for that license certifies at least 10 hours of driving supervised by a licensed driver aged 21 or older. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A04
Upgrading from a provisional license with a clean record earns a $3.50 credit toward the license fee. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A04
A license issued before age 21 is marked Under 21, expires on the 21st birthday, and afterward expires every four years on the birthday. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A04
At age 15 a restricted farm work license, a special medical license or a moped permit may be available after driver education and a road test. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A04
A restricted farm work license lets a teen drive alone for farm work in daylight within 40 miles of the farmhouse, and the restriction can be removed by application after six months with the license and reaching age 16. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A05
Farm work and special medical applicants skip the six-month wait before the road test but still need a permit, a behind-the-wheel completion certificate and a supervised driving log [A05] [A04].
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A05
A special medical license may be issued at 15 when no licensed driver lives in the household and the teen must drive for personal or a relative's medical needs; it carries the restriction code MEDLIM. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A05
A moped permit is available at 15 after a motorized bicycle safety course and the written, vision and road tests, while an electric-assist bicycle needs no test or license but its rider must be at least 15. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0020]

Misconceptions: the permit supervisor must be at least twenty-one only for a teen under eighteen, not for adult permit holders; immediate family members do not count toward provisional passenger limits; the night limit has employment and school-event exceptions; Vanessa's Law delays licensing until eighteen even for a teen who was never licensed.
Mnemonics: permit, provisional, under twenty-one is the GDL ladder; forty with the parent class, fifty without, fifteen at night either way; one passenger then three in the provisional year.
Glossary: GDL means Graduated Driver's Licensing, the staged path for new drivers; provisional license means the restricted second stage; withdrawal notice means the DVS letter listing reinstatement steps; MEDLIM means the special medical license restriction; concurrent course means driver education where classroom and behind-the-wheel overlap.
Dynamic facts: the reinstatement fee, the upgrade credit and other fees are set by the Legislature and can change; confirm current amounts on the DVS fee page.
